newsitem.title: USA: Mistic owner buys Snapple from Quaker for $300 million.
newsitem.headline: Mistic owner buys Snapple from Quaker for $300 million.

text.p: Triarc Companies Inc. , owner of the Mistic and Royal Crown soft drink brands, said Thursday it agreed to buy Quaker Oats Co.'s troubled Snapple drinks unit for $300 million in cash.

Snapple's ready-to-drink teas and juice drinks are a leader in the premium beverage market, with 1996 sales of about $550 million, but the unit has lost money since Quaker bought it on Dec. 6, 1994, for $1.7 billion.
Triarc said it expects to close the deal in the second quarter of this year, subject to customary closing conditions, including government antitrust clearance.

New York-based Triarc, whose businesses include Royal Crown Company and Mistic Brands Inc., fast-food restaurant Arby's Inc., liquefied petroleum gas company National Propane and specialty dyes and chemicals maker C.H. Patrick, has annual revenues of nearly $1 billion.
Quaker, known for its cereals and other prepared foods, also owns Gatorade sports drink.
Quaker's board had previously rejected shareholder proposals that the Chicago-based food giant separate its beverage unit from its core food businesses.
